properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued August 1 at 2:33PM EDT until August 1 at 4:30PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
SMWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm...

* Until 430 PM EDT.

* At 232 PM EDT, strong thunderstorms were located over Palm Bay,
moving northeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, lightning and heavy downpours. Make sure all on
board are wearing life jackets. Return to safe harbor if
possible.

* Locations impacted include...
Spessard Holland Park, Palm Bay, Malabar, Melbourne Beach, and
Indialantic.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.area: Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 1 at 2:29PM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:

miles south of Thomaston, moving southeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Up to 40 mph wind, frequent cloud to ground lightning and
heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect minor damage to tree limbs and blowing around of
light, unsecured objects. Heavy rain may cause temporary
street flooding especially in poor drainage areas.

Locations impacted include...
Butler, Roberta, Salem, Prattsburg, Carsonville, Wesley Church, and
Fickling Mill.
properties.instruction:
People outdoors should seek shelter immediately. If you can hear
thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning. Motorists
should slow down and be prepared for possible loss of control due to
hydroplaning.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 1 at 2:26PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
At 224 PM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms near
Palm Bay, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Palm Bay, Melbourne, Satellite Beach, Malabar, and Indialantic.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Conditions are favorable for the development of weak, brief funnel
clouds at the coast. On rare occasions they can briefly touch down,
producing wind gusts over 50 mph. If a funnel cloud is spotted move
indoors and report your sighting to the National Weather Service.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

These storms may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional
information and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.
properties.area: Inland Southern Brevard; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued August 1 at 2:22PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 0-20 nm...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm...

At 216 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated developing thunderstorms,
capable of producing winds to around 33 knots. These thunderstorms
will push off of the coast through mid to late afternoon, and will
move east or northeast at 10 to 15 knots. With the sea breeze pinned
at the coast, storms will likely strengthen rapidly at the coast or
just off of the coast creating hazardous conditions for boaters.
Keep an eye to the sky westward for developing and approaching
storms.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 33 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Waterspouts are possible with this
activity near the coast this afternoon. Remain on the alert in case
warnings are issued for waterspout development.

Strong thunderstorms this afternoon will likely produce winds in
excess of 34 knots, and are likely to pose a serious hazard for
boaters. A special marine warning will likely be required when these
strong thunderstorms reach the nearshore waters. Boaters should
consider heading for shore before these strong thunderstorms arrive.
properties.area: Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm; Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 0-20 nm
